A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GOAT research despite the revised title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. The conditional-generation material can be matched across its relocation from the appendix to the main text.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices G–H report original GOAT generation results on QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, component ablations, transport costs, and property-conditioned generation.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices G–H retain original generation experiments and report additional parameter ablations, conditional-generation comparisons, and noise-to-molecule distances.

M1.justification: v2 Equation 3 introduces adjustable lambda and 1-lambda weights for coordinate and feature transport costs, extending v1's unweighted Equation 5. The selected lambda=0.5 preserves equal relative weighting. The autoencoder, alignment procedures, flow loss, purification, and Appendix C algorithm steps otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate unconditional generation on QM9 and GEOM-DRUG and conditional QM9 generation for the same six properties: alpha, energy gap, HOMO energy, LUMO energy, dipole moment, and heat capacity. Added efficiency and distance analyses do not introduce another dataset or generation task.

E2.justification: The added noise-distance comparison evaluates EDM and GeoLDM alongside EquiFM in v2 Table 7, broadening comparator participation beyond the EquiFM-only external comparison in v1's transport-cost Figure 3. The principal unconditional and conditional generation baseline rosters remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces S-Time in place of ordinary per-generated-molecule timing and reports additional conditional settings: 100 steps for EquiFM and GeoBFN and 200 steps for GOAT. New diagnostics introduce lambda variation, an autoencoder-removal control, and noise-distance measurements. Existing splits, 10K evaluation samples, architectures, and training budgets remain unchanged. S-Time is inconsistently defined as molecules/time but interpreted as seconds per significant molecule.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands component and mechanism analysis. Table 4 adds an autoencoder ablation and a five-value lambda sweep to the existing OMT/ODT ablations. Table 7 adds noise-to-generated-molecule distances across both datasets and component variants, while Figure 4 examines conditional quality versus sampling steps. The earlier iterative-transport analysis and GeoBFN sampling-step sweep are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain point-estimate reporting; the metric called Significance measures generation quality, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Main-table GOAT QM9 atom stability, validity, and significance change from 98.4/90.9/70.8 to 99.2/92.9/72.3; GEOM-DRUG atom stability and validity change from 81.8/96.0 to 84.8/96.2. v2 adds conditional results at additional step budgets, parameter/component results, and distance measurements, and revises appendix entries. The six-property GeoBFN 500-step row is no longer fully reported, although its alpha result remains in Figure 4. These are reported revisions, not established performance gains: settings differ for added rows, and v2 Table 5 still reports GOAT QM9 stability/validity as 98.4/90.0.

T1.justification: The formal optimal-transport cost changes from an unweighted sum in v1 Equation 5 to a lambda-weighted definition in v2 Equation 3. Theorem 3.1, the symmetry definitions, and the Appendix B derivation otherwise remain unchanged. The appendix proof still uses the unweighted cost; no corresponding new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract now describes an estimated optimal transport plan and a non-increasing cost guarantee, rather than simply an optimal path and cost reduction. It also explicitly attributes the guarantee to coupling estimation and purification. The central contribution and roughly twofold sampling-speed claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds the hypothesis that equal modality weights reflect the generative model's actual transport cost and interprets the new noise-distance results as supporting its speed mechanism. Conditional-generation discussion emphasizes the quality–efficiency tradeoff. Training-cost limitations and the qualification that latent-space optimality does not guarantee original-space optimality already appear in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-repository pointers in the abstract and Appendix F and documents lambda=0.5 as the selected weighting. Existing EGNN dimensions, optimizer settings, epoch counts, 100K purified coupling pairs, hardware, and training-time disclosures are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repositories' contents or availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jung et al. (2024), Conditional Synthesis of 3D Molecules with Time Correction Sampler, to the introduction and references. The substantive related-work discussion and positioning against EquiFM remain largely unchanged. Citation-style and publication-year updates do not represent additional research comparisons.

P1.justification: The title and terminology shift from unified toward joint/jointly, with localized abstract, method, and results edits. Conditional-generation details move from Appendix H into Section 4.2, the property glossary is omitted, and Appendix H now presents distances. The overall section sequence and most explanatory prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental displays: the combined benchmark table becomes separate Tables 1–2 with S-Time, the conditional table moves and expands beside new Figure 4, and the ablation table gains rows and columns. Table 7 is new. The ICLR template changes typography and headers; existing plots are resized or relocated, and the unchanged molecule galleries are consolidated onto one page.

improvement.justification: Matched-step conditional comparisons, expanded component diagnostics, and code pointers improve evaluability. However, the new S-Time definition conflicts with its interpretation and optimization direction. Revised main-table results also introduce discrepancies: v2 reports QM9 GOAT atom stability as 99.2 in Table 1 but 98.4 in Table 5, whereas v1 agreed on 98.4. Some earlier inconsistencies are corrected, while others persist. Because the gains coexist with new ambiguities affecting central efficiency and quality evidence, a reliable net improvement cannot be established.
